cues.f1|Master equation: Thrust over weight = drag over weight + P_s/V. Inside the brace: qS/(βW) times the polar evaluated at C_L = nβW/(qS); α and β scale it.
cues.f1|Simplified master equation: Parasite term qC_D0/(βW/S) falls with W/S, induced term K₁n²β(W/S)/q rises; climb adds (1/V)dh/dt, acceleration adds (1/g)dV/dt.
cues.f1|Stall and landing constraint: Lift equals weight at C_Lmax: W/S = ½ρV²C_Lmax, divided by β. A vertical wall on the diagram, feasible to its left.
cues.f1|Takeoff constraint: Ground roll s = V²/(2a) with a = gT/W and V_TO = k_TO V_stall: T/W is a straight line through the origin in W/S.
cues.f1|Constant-speed bucket: One term falls and one rises with W/S: the minimum is where they are equal, and the sum there is 2√(product) = 2n√(K₁C_D0).
cues.f2|Breguet range (jet): Jet fuel flow follows thrust, so V appears: c_t has units of 1/time, so V/c_t is a length. Log of start over end weight.
cues.f2|Breguet range (propeller): Propeller c_p is fuel per unit energy; η_p/c_p is already a length, so the speed term drops away. Log of start over end weight.
cues.f2|Jet endurance: Range over speed: time aloft = (1/c_t)(L/D)ln(W_i/W_f), best at (L/D)max for a jet.
cues.f2|Maximum lift-to-drag: Best L/D where parasite equals induced: C_D0 = KC_L², so C_L* = √(C_D0/K), C_D = 2C_D0, and L/D = 1/(2√(KC_D0)).
cues.f2|Rate of climb: Climb rate is excess power per unit weight: power available minus power required, divided by W, equals V sin γ.
cues.f2|Takeoff ground roll: 1.44 = 1.2², from liftoff at 1.2V_stall; distance grows with W² (speed squared and lower acceleration both scale with W).
cues.f3|Stall boundary: Lift at C_Lmax divided by weight: a parabola in V_e starting at the origin and reaching n = 1 at V_S1.
cues.f3|Equivalent airspeed: Same dynamic pressure: ½ρV² = ½ρ₀V_e², so V_e = V√σ, smaller than true airspeed at altitude.
cues.f3|Maneuvering (corner) speed: Stall parabola n = (V/V_S1)² meets the n_max line: set n = n_max and solve for V.
cues.f3|Gust load factor: ΔL = ½ρ₀V_e²Sa(U_de/V_e) divided by W, times alleviation K_g; Δn grows linearly with V_e and falls with W/S.
cues.f3|FAR 25 limit load factors: 2.1 plus 24 thousand over (W plus 10 thousand), W in pounds; clamp between 2.5 and 3.8; the negative limit is −1.
cues.f3|Ultimate load: Factor of safety 1.5 on the limit load.
cues.f4|Uninstalled thrust: Momentum out minus momentum in, plus pressure thrust acting on the exit area.
cues.f4|Propulsive efficiency: Limiting case: V_e approaching V₀ gives η_p approaching 1 (and thrust approaching 0). A slower jet is a more efficient jet.
cues.f4|Ideal Brayton thermal efficiency: Efficiency set by the total temperature ratio of compression: ram τ_r times compressor τ_c. More compression, higher η_th.
cues.f4|Overall efficiency and TSFC: Useful power FV₀ over fuel energy rate ṁ_f h_PR equals η_th η_p. TSFC is fuel flow per unit thrust.
cues.f4|Component isentropic efficiency: Compressor: ideal work on top (smaller). Turbine: ideal work on the bottom (larger). Both ratios stay below 1.
cues.f4|Stagnation relations: T_t/T = 1 + ((γ − 1)/2)M²; raise that ratio to γ/(γ − 1) for the isentropic pressure ratio.
cues.f5|Kutta-Joukowski theorem: Lift per span = density × speed × circulation. Units: kg/m³ · m/s · m²/s = N/m.
cues.f5|Thin airfoil theory: Slope 2π per radian (about 0.11 per degree), shifted by the zero-lift angle; aerodynamic center at the quarter chord.
cues.f5|Induced drag: C_L squared over π e AR; e = 1 for elliptic loading, the minimum. Induced angle = C_L/(πAR).
cues.f5|Finite wing lift slope: Downwash softens the slope: as AR grows large, a approaches a₀.
cues.f5|Prandtl-Glauert correction: Compressibility amplifies C_p by 1/β with β = √(1 − M∞²); valid for subsonic flow below critical Mach.
cues.f5|Sweep and normal Mach: The wing responds to the velocity component normal to its swept quarter-chord line: M cos Λ, so sweep raises critical Mach.
cues.f6|Momentum theory hover: The far wake speeds up to twice the disk velocity: T = ṁ·2v_i with ṁ = ρAv_i, so T = 2ρAv_i².
cues.f6|Ideal hover power: Power = thrust × induced velocity; substitute v_i = √(T/(2ρA)) to get T^(3/2)/√(2ρA).
cues.f6|Figure of merit: Ideal over actual power, between 0 and 1, typically about 0.7 to 0.8 for a good rotor.
cues.f6|Thrust coefficient: Thrust normalised by ρA times tip speed squared; blade element gives (σa/2)(θ₀/3 − λ/2).
cues.f6|Advance ratio and tip speeds: Forward speed over tip speed. The advancing tip adds V, the retreating tip subtracts V.
cues.f6|Induced velocity in fast forward flig: Glauert: mass flow through the disk becomes ρAV at high speed, so v_i ≈ T/(2ρAV), falling as V grows.
cues.f7|Takeoff weight sizing: Crew and payload divided by the fraction left after fuel and empty weight fractions are subtracted from 1.
cues.f7|Empty weight fraction: Statistical power law: C is a small negative exponent, so W_e/W₀ falls slowly with size; K_vs covers variable sweep.
cues.f7|Fuel fraction: Multiply the segment fractions; 1 minus the product is fuel burned; × 1.06 adds 6% reserve and trapped fuel.
cues.f7|Cruise and loiter fractions: Breguet solved for weight ratio: cruise exponent −Rc/(V L/D), loiter exponent −Ec/(L/D).
cues.f7|Divergence dynamic pressure: Torsional stiffness over the aerodynamic twisting lever: offset e from ac to elastic axis times lift slope a times area S.
cues.f7|Control reversal dynamic pressure: Stiffness over the flap twisting moment; C_Mδ is negative, so the leading minus sign gives a positive q_R.
cues.f8|Tangential equation: Along the path: thrust component T cos(α + ε) minus drag minus W sin γ equals mass times acceleration.
cues.f8|Normal equation: Perpendicular to the path: centripetal mV dγ/dt from lift plus T sin(α + ε) minus W cos γ.
cues.f8|Path kinematics: Resolve velocity along the path angle: vertical V sin γ, horizontal V cos γ.
cues.f8|Level coordinated turn: Vertical lift component L cos φ = W gives n = 1/cos φ; the horizontal component W√(n² − 1) supplies centripetal force.
cues.f8|Vertical pull-up: At the bottom, lift supplies weight plus centripetal force: L − W = mV²/R.
cues.f8|Energy height and excess power: Total energy per unit weight: altitude plus kinetic head V²/(2g); P_s is its time rate.
cues.f9|Parabolic drag polar: A parabola in C_L: parasite plus induced, with K = 1/(πeAR).
cues.f9|Component drag buildup: Each component: friction × form factor × interference × wetted area, summed, over S_ref, plus miscellaneous and leakage/protuberance.
cues.f9|Skin friction coefficients: Laminar Blasius 1.328/√Re; turbulent uses log₁₀Re to the 2.58 with a compressibility factor (1 + 0.144M²)^0.65.
cues.f9|Wing form factor: Thickness bracket (t/c term with max thickness location, plus 100(t/c)⁴) times a Mach and sweep correction.
cues.f9|Flap lift increment: Airfoil increment × 0.9 × flapped area fraction × cosine of hinge-line sweep.
cues.f9|Stall speed: Lift = weight at C_Lmax: V_stall = √(2W/(ρSC_Lmax)); in a pull-up the wing carries nW, so multiply W by n.
cues.f10|Pitch stiffness and static margin: C_mα = −C_Lα·SM: CG ahead of the neutral point gives positive SM and negative C_mα, a stable aircraft.
cues.f10|Stick-fixed neutral point: Wing-body ac moved aft by η × tail volume × lift slope ratio × (1 − downwash gradient).
cues.f10|Tail volume coefficients: Tail area × tail arm over wing area × reference length: c̄ for the horizontal tail, span b for the vertical tail.
cues.f10|Trim elevator deflection: Two equations, two unknowns (α, δ_e): Cramer's rule; the denominator is the determinant of [[C_Lα, C_Lδe],[C_mα, C_mδe]].
cues.f10|Lateral-directional static stability: Weathercock: positive C_nβ turns the nose into the wind. Dihedral: sideslip rolls the aircraft away from the wind, C_lβ negative.
cues.f10|Phugoid approximation: Lanchester: ω = √2 g/V, so the period grows with speed, about 0.45V seconds with V in m/s.
